name: 영어 뇌 만들기 문장 5개 : Part 12 (I wish you had asked me earlier/I don’t know. I can’t think of anything./ I hope she isn’t in (any kind of) trouble/There (really)is nothing like a hot bowl of ramyun on a day like this.)

keywords.en: I wish you had asked me earlier.
bold_words: had asked

keywords.ko: should’ve , why didn’t you 를 사용하면 좀 탓하는 뉘앙스가 강함.

keywords.en: I don’t know. I can’t think of anything.
keywords.ko: 글쎄, 생각나는 게 없는데, 떠오르는 게 없는데.
딱히 떠오르는 게 없다.(내가 이전에 들었던 것과 연결되지 않는다.)

keywords.en: I hope she isn’t in (any kind of) trouble.
Why can’t I go back to the previous page?
Why won’t it let me go back to the previous page?
bold_words: Why won’t it let me

keywords.en: It’s not letting me go back to the previous page.
There (really)is nothing like a hot bowl of ramyun on a day like this.
keywords.ko: 역시 이런 날에는 따뜻한 라면 한 그릇만한 게 없지

keywords.en: I wish you had asked me earlier.
I don’t know. I can’t think of anything.
I hope she isn’t in any kind of trouble.
Why can’t I go back to the previous page?
Why won’t it let me go back to the previous page?
It’s not letting me go back to the previous page.
There (really) is nothing like a hot bowl of ramyun on a day like this.

my_sentences.ko: I wish + 주어 + had p.p.

과거에 이미 일어난(혹은 일어나지 않은) 일에 대한 ‘아쉬움과 유감’을 표현하는 가정법 과거완료 구문입니다. You should have asked me나 Why didn't you ask me?는 "왜 안 물어봤어?", "물어봤어야지"처럼 상대방을 직접 탓하거나 책망하는 느낌을 주기 쉽습니다. 반면 I wish you had asked me는 "물어봤으면 (내가 도와줄 수 있었을 텐데) 아쉽다"처럼 내 감정(아쉬움)에 초점이 맞춰져 훨씬 부드럽습니다.

my_sentences.en: I wish I had known about this place sooner.
my_sentences.ko: (이 장소를 좀 더 일찍 알았더라면 좋았을 텐데.)
bold_words: I wish I had known about this place sooner.

my_sentences.en: I wish you had told me before you left.
my_sentences.ko: (출발하기 전에 나한테 미리 말해줬으면 좋았을 텐데.)
bold_words: I wish you had told me before you left.

my_sentences.en: I wish I hadn't stayed up so late last night.
my_sentences.ko: (어젯밤에 그렇게 늦게까지 깨어있지 말았어야 했는데.)
bold_words: I wish I hadn't stayed up so late last night.

my_sentences.en: I wish we had booked the tickets in advance.
my_sentences.ko: (우리가 티켓을 미리 예매해 뒀더라면 좋았을 텐데.)
bold_words: I wish we had booked the tickets in advance.

my_sentences.en: I wish you had joined us for dinner.
my_sentences.ko: (너도 저녁 식사에 같이 왔으면 정말 좋았을 텐데.)
bold_words: I wish you had joined us for dinner.

my_sentences.en: That doesn't ring a bell
my_sentences.ko: 누군가 이름, 장소, 사건 등을 언급했을 때 ‘기억이나 경험의 종을 울리지 않는다’, 즉 "들어본 기억이 없다", "금시초문이다", "전혀 낯익지 않다"는 뜻입니다.
bold_words: That doesn't ring a bell

my_sentences.en: I can't think of anything
my_sentences.ko: 머릿속에서 아이디어, 해결책, 사례 등을 끄집어내려 해도 ‘아무것도 떠오르지 않는다’는 뜻입니다.
bold_words: I can't think of anything

my_sentences.en: His name sounds familiar, but his face doesn't ring a bell.
my_sentences.ko: (이름은 낯이 익은데, 얼굴은 전혀 기억이 안 나.)
bold_words: His name sounds familiar, but his face doesn't ring a bell.

my_sentences.en: "Do you remember the cafe we went to last year?"
my_sentences.ko: "우리 작년에 갔던 그 카페 기억나?"
bold_words: "Do you remember the cafe we went to last year?"

my_sentences.en: "Sorry, that doesn't ring a bell."
my_sentences.ko: "미안, 전혀 기억 안 나.")
bold_words: "Sorry, that doesn't ring a bell."

my_sentences.en: I'm trying to figure out a gift for Sarah, but I can't think of anything.
my_sentences.ko: (사라 줄 선물을 생각 중인데, 마땅히 떠오르는 게 없어.)
bold_words: I'm trying to figure out a gift for Sarah, but I can't think of anything.

my_sentences.en: I can't think of anything else to add to this report.
my_sentences.ko: (이 보고서에 더 추가할 만한 내용이 생각이 안 나.)
bold_words: I can't think of anything else to add to this report.

my_sentences.en: Does the title of that movie ring a bell to you?
my_sentences.ko: (그 영화 제목 들어본 적 있어? 기억나?)
bold_words: Does the title of that movie ring a bell to you?

my_sentences.en: be in trouble
my_sentences.ko: 곤란한 처지에 놓이거나 문제/사고에 휘말린 상태입니다.
bold_words: be in trouble

my_sentences.en: any kind of
my_sentences.ko: 부정문이나 의문문에서 명사 앞에 붙여 ‘어떤 종류든, 무슨 문제든 간에’라는 뜻으로 불안감이나 강조를 나타냅니다.
bold_words: any kind of

my_sentences.en: I hope (she isn't...):
my_sentences.ko: "그녀가 ~가 아니기를 바란다"는 뜻으로, 나쁜 일이 일어나지 않았으면 하는 걱정 어린 바람을 전할 때 씁니다.
bold_words: I hope (she isn't...)

my_sentences.en: I hope we aren't in any kind of trouble for parking here.
my_sentences.ko: (여기 주차했다고 무슨 문제 생기는 건 아니었으면 좋겠네.)
bold_words: I hope we aren't in any kind of trouble for parking here.

my_sentences.en: He didn't show up today; I hope he isn't in trouble.
my_sentences.ko: (그 친구 오늘 안 나왔던데, 무슨 일 생긴 건 아니어야 할 텐데.)
bold_words: He didn't show up today; I hope he isn't in trouble.

my_sentences.en: If you need help, just tell me. I don't want you to be in trouble.
my_sentences.ko: (도움이 필요하면 그냥 말해. 네가 곤란해지는 건 원치 않아.)
bold_words: If you need help, just tell me. I don't want you to be in trouble.

my_sentences.en: Make sure you double-check the figures so we won't get into any kind of trouble.
my_sentences.ko: (문제 생기지 않도록 수치 꼭 다시 확인해 둬.)
bold_words: Make sure you double-check the figures so we won't get into any kind of trouble.

my_sentences.en: I hope this delay doesn't cause any kind of trouble for the team.
my_sentences.ko: (이 지연 때문에 팀에 무슨 문제라도 생기지 않았으면 좋겠어.)
bold_words: I hope this delay doesn't cause any kind of trouble for the team.

my_sentences.en: It's not letting me ~, Why won't it let me ~?
my_sentences.ko: 기기나 시스템(앱, 웹사이트, 스마트폰 등)을 주어로 삼아 "이 시스템이 나에게 ~하는 것을 허락하지 않는다"는 영어식 물주구문(사람이 아닌 사물이 주어인 문장)입니다.
bold_words: It's not letting me ~,  Why won't it let me ~?

my_sentences.ko: I can't log in이라고 하면 내가 비밀번호를 잊어버렸거나 조작을 못 해서일 수도 있지만, It's not letting me log in이라고 하면 "시스템 오류나 버그 때문에 안 들어가지네"라는 뉘앙스가 명확해집니다.

my_sentences.en: It's not letting me upload this file.
my_sentences.ko: (이 파일이 업로드가 안 되네.)
bold_words: It's not letting me upload this file.

my_sentences.en: Why won't it let me submit the form?
my_sentences.ko: (왜 제출 버튼이 안 먹히지? / 왜 제출이 안 되지?)
bold_words: Why won't it let me submit the form?

my_sentences.en: The app is not letting me reset my password.
my_sentences.ko: (앱에서 비밀번호 재설정이 계속 안 돼.)
bold_words: The app is not letting me reset my password.

my_sentences.en: Why won't this screen let me scroll down?
my_sentences.ko: (화면이 왜 아래로 안 내려가지?)
bold_words: Why won't this screen let me scroll down?

my_sentences.en: My phone is not letting me connect to the Wi-Fi.
my_sentences.ko: (핸드폰 와이파이 연결이 안 되네.)
bold_words: My phone is not letting me connect to the Wi-Fi.

my_sentences.en: There is nothing like [n]:
my_sentences.ko: "~만한 게 없다", "~가 최고다"라는 뜻의 최상급 대체 찬사 표현입니다.
bold_words: There is nothing like [n]

my_sentences.en: on a day like this
my_sentences.ko: "이런 날에는" (비 오는 날, 유난히 추운 날, 스트레스 받는 날 등 특정 분위기나 날씨).
bold_words: on a day like this

my_sentences.en: There is nothing like an iced coffee on a day like this.
my_sentences.ko: (오늘 같은 날에는 시원한 아이스 커피만 한 게 없지.)
bold_words: There is nothing like an iced coffee on a day like this.

my_sentences.en: There is nothing like a warm bath after a long day at work.
my_sentences.ko: (힘든 하루를 마치고 받는 따뜻한 반신욕만 한 게 없어.)
bold_words: There is nothing like a warm bath after a long day at work.

my_sentences.en: There is really nothing like homemade soup when you're feeling sick.
my_sentences.ko: (몸이 으슬으슬 아플 때는 집에서 끓인 국물 요리만 한 게 없지.)
bold_words: There is really nothing like homemade soup when you're feeling sick.

my_sentences.en: On a day like this, there is nothing like staying home and watching movies.
my_sentences.ko: (이런 날씨에는 집에서 뒹굴거리며 영화 보는 게 최고야.)
bold_words: On a day like this, there is nothing like staying home and watching movies.

my_sentences.en: There is nothing like a cold beer after a tough workout.
my_sentences.ko: (격한 운동 뒤에 마시는 시원한 맥주 한 잔만 한 게 없지.)
bold_words: There is nothing like a cold beer after a tough workout.
